name: fort
comment: Rule shapes test/highlight_test.py reads: see editors/README.md.

comment.comment: // to the end of the line is the only comment form (D2.2).
comment.name: comment.line.double-slash.fort

block-comment.comment: The adjacent pair /* is a lexical error, not a comment (D2.2).
block-comment.name: invalid.illegal.block-comment.fort

string.comment: "..." with escapes; the run to the newline is the error D2.9 makes it.
string.name: string.quoted.double.fort

string-unterminated.comment: A string that reaches the newline is an error, so its tail is painted (D2.9).
string-unterminated.name: invalid.illegal.unterminated-string.fort

char.comment: 'x' is one printable ASCII byte other than ' and \, or one escape (D2.7).
char.name: string.quoted.single.fort

char-invalid.comment: Anything else between two quotes is not a char literal (D2.7, D2.8).
char-invalid.name: invalid.illegal.character.fort

escape.comment: The escapes are \n \t \r \0 \\ \' \" and \xHH, two hex digits (D2.8).
escape.name: constant.character.escape.fort

escape-invalid.comment: Anything else after a backslash is an error (D2.8).
escape-invalid.name: invalid.illegal.escape.fort

number-leading-zero.comment: A decimal other than 0 may not start with 0, and _ sits between digits (D2.5).
number-leading-zero.name: invalid.illegal.numeric.fort

number-float-fraction.comment: digits . digits with an optional exponent; 1. and .5 are not literals (D2.6).
number-float-fraction.name: constant.numeric.float.fort

reserved.comment: Reserved for future use and usable nowhere, so it is painted wrong (D2.4).
reserved.name: invalid.illegal.reserved.fort

keyword-control.comment: Control flow and the statements that carry it (D2.4).
keyword-control.name: keyword.control.fort

keyword-import.comment: import path, . for a segment or a symbol and as for an alias (D2.4, D9.3).
keyword-import.name: keyword.control.import.fort

keyword-expression.comment: cast(e, T), new(T), new(T, n) and sizeof(T) are keyword-led (D2.4).
keyword-expression.name: keyword.operator.word.fort

storage-primitive.comment: The primitive type names, string and void (D2.4, D3.1).
storage-primitive.name: storage.type.primitive.fort

storage-mut.comment: mut marks the storage of the type element it follows, anywhere (D5.3).
storage-mut.name: storage.modifier.mut.fort

storage-own.comment: own follows a * or an @, or string, and marks it owning (D17.2).
storage-own.name: storage.modifier.own.fort

storage-modifier.comment: extern on a declaration, noreturn on a return type (D2.4).
storage-modifier.name: storage.modifier.fort

declaration-type.comment: struct name and enum name introduce a type name (D3.8, D3.9).

keyword-fn.comment: fn introduces a function definition and a function type (D3.10).
keyword-fn.name: storage.type.function.fort

qualified-type.comment: Heuristic: mod.name in a type position is a module and a type (D9.4); `as` only ever follows an import path, whose separator is the same dot (D9.1).

type-before-suffix.comment: Heuristic: an identifier directly before * or @ is a base type (D3.6).

type-before-marker.comment: Heuristic: an identifier before mut or own is what they mark (D5.3, D17.2).

type-before-name.comment: Heuristic: an identifier before a name that ends a declarator (D8.2).

entity-function.comment: An identifier directly before ( is a definition or a call (D8.1).

entity-type-literal.comment: An identifier directly before { is the type of a literal (D3.8).

operator-three.comment: Longest match wins, so the three-byte operators come first (D2.10).
operator-three.name: keyword.operator.assignment.fort

operator-wrapping.comment: % is never a prefix operator, so +% is unambiguous (D2.10).
operator-wrapping.name: keyword.operator.arithmetic.wrapping.fort

operator-variadic.comment: ... marks a C extern tail and matches before .. (D2.10, D9.8).
operator-variadic.name: keyword.operator.variadic.fort

operator-range.comment: .. is the span range, and 1..5 lexes as 1 .. 5 (D2.10, D6.9).
operator-range.name: keyword.operator.range.fort

operator-span.comment: @ is the span suffix of a type (D3.5, D3.6).
operator-span.name: keyword.operator.span.fort

operator-accessor-one.comment: A field, a module path separator, a module member, an enum member (D9.1, D9.4).
operator-accessor-one.name: keyword.operator.accessor.fort

punctuation-colon.comment: The colon of a case label and of the conditional (D2.10).
punctuation-colon.name: punctuation.separator.colon.fort

identifier.comment: Identifiers are [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]* (D2.3); a regex cannot type them.
identifier.name: variable.other.fort
